We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and PCKL and have gone through the documents on record. The Petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking clarification of the findings of the Commission in Issue No.6 in the order dated 13.1.2023 in Petition No.155/MP/2019, wherein the Commission specified a formula 13. The Petitioner filed Petition No.155/MP/2019 for adjudication of the disputes between the Petitioner and the Respondents, and one of the disputes raised in the petition was regarding the computation of energy charges due to the disallowance of the actual landed cost of the coal procured on a spot basis. The prayers made by the Petitioner in Petition No.155/MP/2019 in this regard are as follows: 14. Taking into consideration the submissions made by the Petitioner and Respondents with respect to energy charges, the Commission framed the following issue in Petition No.155/MP/2019: 15. Thus, one of the prayers made by the Petitioner in Petition No.155/MP/2019 was for allowance of the actual coal cost procured through the spot market along with the Carrying Cost. The Petitioner did not distinguish between the coal procured from the “sister companies” and the coal procured from “entities other than the sister companies” in Petition No.155/MP/2019. Accordingly, the only issue before the Commission was whether the Petitioner was entitled to recover the actual cost of coal procured from the spot market. Therefore, the Commission did not distinguish between the coal procured from the “sister companies” and from “entities other than the sister companies” in its findings in the order dated 13.1.2023. Nilima Mandal, (2008) 17 SCC 491 (Para 17), the Petitioner has submitted that a judgment cannot be interpreted to have rendered a finding on fact/ issue which was not raised in pleadings. Applying this legal principle to the facts of this case, since Respondents had raised no aspersions regarding the Petitioner’s coal procurement from ‘entities other than the sister companies’, the benchmark energy charges formula laid down cannot be read to apply to the Petitioner’s coal procurement from ‘entities other than the sister companies’. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions. We have already made it clear (in paragraph 17) that the Commission’s findings in the order dated 13.1.2023 are applicable to the coal procured from the Petitioner’s “sister companies” and “entities other than the sister companies” and there is no distinction made on the basis of the source of coal. Therefore, the Petitioner’s claim that, as no aspersions were cast on the coal procured from ‘entities other than sister companies’, the formula specified cannot be made applicable to the Petitioner’s coal procurement from ‘entities other than the sister companies’ does not hold good.
